search_bias: Autonomous-scientist systems and empirical research-agent papers; strongest quantitative primary sources first, then citation/failure branching. This run resumed only the clean_g1 checkpoint, followed its ASI-Bench/AIRS-Bench frontier, and then branched into ARAC-Bench, ResearchAgent, data-to-paper, and MLReplicate.

checked_sources.title: Towards end-to-end automation of AI research
ASI-Bench: At the Dawn of Artificial Superintelligence
AIRS-Bench: a Suite of Tasks for Frontier AI Research Science Agents
ARAC: Benchmarking Auto-Research's Alignment and Completeness on End-to-End Researchs
ResearchAgent: Iterative Research Idea Generation over Scientific Literature with Large Language Models
MLReplicate: Benchmarking Autonomous Research Systems for Machine Learning Reproducibility
ResearchClawBench: A Benchmark for End-to-End Autonomous Scientific Research
Data-to-paper: autonomous research from data to manuscript

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Full-artifact scientific audit: evaluate execution traces, code, data provenance, and manuscript claims together rather than paper text alone.
evidence: Prior clean checkpoint: controlled audit of Agent Laboratory and AI Scientist-v2 reported paper-only pitfall detection around 55% accuracy / 0.51 F1 versus about 82% / 0.81 when traces and code were available.

MLReplicate found automated overall paper ratings weakly aligned with expert human judgment (Pearson r=0.29; Spearman rho=0.40 across 10 jointly evaluated papers) and fabricated/unsupported claims in 59% of automated acceptances.
MLReplicate explicitly notes a major limitation: it evaluated manuscripts without validating underlying experiments, strengthening the case that manuscript-only review is structurally insufficient.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Autonomous ML/scientific-research systems; strongest evidence supports audit necessity, not a particular online auditor implementation.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need randomized evidence that an online full-artifact audit improves end-to-end discovery rather than only post-hoc detection.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Parallel best-first / tree-based experimentation with checkpointed candidate branches instead of one-shot research generation.
evidence: AIRS-Bench reports much stronger aggregate normalized scores for Greedy best-first search than One-Shot over easy/medium/hard tasks; under one main transform Greedy scores 0.73/0.48/0.30 vs One-Shot 0.10/0.18/0.05 and ReAct 0.50/0.31/0.15.
AIRS-Bench valid-submission rates are very high for several Greedy configurations (for example 0.970 gpt-oss-120b, 0.950 o3-mini) compared with many One-Shot configurations.
Nature's AI Scientist uses staged tree search across preliminary investigation, hyperparameter tuning, agenda execution and ablation; experimental-node scaling correlates with higher review score.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Executable ML research tasks. Scaffold evidence is strongest on easy-to-hard AIRS tasks, not uniformly on expert tasks.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: AIRS expert slice can favor ReAct under one transform (0.10 vs Greedy 0.04), and model/scaffold availability is not fully matched; extract same-model budget-matched pairs before causal promotion.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Explicit research-procedure synthesis / protocol compilation stage: convert a chosen method into a complete executable procedure before experimentation.
evidence: ASI-Bench's guidance gradient isolates a 21.82-point average drop from full method+procedure guidance (B1 50.91) to method guidance without detailed procedure (B2 29.10).
Removing the method hint as well (B2 29.10 to B3 26.62) costs only another 2.48 points, so procedure completion is a substantially larger diagnosed bottleneck than method selection in this benchmark.

B2 is also the most expensive condition: roughly 6.91M tokens and 49.7 minutes per task, about +59% tokens and +32% time versus B1, suggesting incomplete method hints can induce expensive search without supplying executable procedural structure.
MLReplicate Tiny Scientist logs show upstream plan/data-modality mismatch cascades into futile coder retries; only low-level API mismatch is reliably self-corrected.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Project-level scientific tasks in ASI-Bench plus ML execution logs. Supports a bottleneck diagnosis; the optimal procedure compiler architecture remains unknown.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need intervention studies comparing explicit protocol compilation/validation against equal-budget iterative execution.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Plan–execution–evidence consistency verifier with bidirectional repair, checking that planned data/method contracts match code and that manuscript claims match logged results.
evidence: ResearchClawBench localizes major failures to experimental protocol mismatch, evidence mismatch, and missing scientific core rather than mostly execution/reporting failures.

MLReplicate Tiny Scientist failure taxonomy identifies cross-modal hallucination and logical implementation drift as dominant high-blast-radius failures; authors state these cannot be repaired by coder self-correction alone and require bidirectional verification between planning and execution.
MLReplicate human reviewers found pervasive fabricated/unsupported claims despite automated acceptance, reinforcing the need for evidence-to-claim checks.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Failure-derived intervention hypothesis across ML research-agent systems.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need clean ablation of verifier placement, thresholds, and repair policy.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Relevant-reference retrieval plus bounded multi-agent refinement for research-idea construction.
evidence: ResearchAgent full system scores 4.52/4.28/4.18 on Problem/Method/Experiment versus 4.20/4.03/3.92 without both entities and references.

Removing relevant references hurts more than removing cross-domain entities (w/o references 4.26/4.08/3.97; w/o entities 4.35/4.13/4.02), indicating reference grounding is the stronger knowledge source in this setup.
Iterative refinement saturates after about three iterations, arguing for bounded refinement rather than unbounded reviewer loops.
Benefits depend on base model: GPT-4 and several capable open models improve, while GPT-3.5 and Mixtral show little or inconsistent gain.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Research-idea generation over scientific literature, not full end-to-end autonomous experimentation.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need end-to-end tests linking better idea scores to executable, reproducible discoveries.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Structured academic skill/tool packages as proposal-and-synthesis support, while treating experiment reasoning as a separate unsolved bottleneck.
evidence: ARAC-Bench matched ClaudeCode baseline 54.53 against +AR-Skill 61.21 (+12.25%), +Arbor 59.16 (+8.49%), +AIR-Skill 58.98 (+8.16%), and +SA-Skill 58.09 (+6.53%).
AR-Skill especially improves Related +23.35%, Idea +22.25%, Basic +38.07%, Methodological +32.28%, while Benchmark falls 6.28% and Coding falls 2.13%.

ARAC authors report these packages improve Proposal and Synthesis but not Experiment, consistent with tools helping retrieval/validation/logical checking without closing core experimental-reasoning gaps.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: One benchmark and ClaudeCode-based matched additions; relevant to tool modularization, not evidence that skill packages solve autonomous science.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need replication across models/domains and exact decomposition of which skill components cause the gains.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Abstract inspiration/cognitive-pivot signals that preserve a high-level clue while hiding the ground-truth solution, to trigger structured proposal reasoning.
evidence: ARAC-Bench removing Inspiration while retaining domain background reduces average Idea score from 14.02 to 11.14 (-20.54%) across 11 systems.
Drop is larger for some stronger systems, e.g. AutoResearchClaw -30.38%, versus EvoScientist -11.58%, suggesting capable systems exploit sparse high-level pivots nonlinearly.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Proposal-stage benchmark ablation; Inspiration is a benchmark input condition, not yet a proven autonomous mechanism for discovering its own pivots.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Key missing step is self-generation/selection of valid inspiration pivots without leaking target solutions or anchoring on misleading clues.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Programmatic claim provenance: data-chained manuscripts that backtrace narrative claims to analysis code and source data.
evidence: Data-to-paper reports autonomous recapitulation of peer-reviewed biomedical findings without major errors in roughly 80–90% of simple-goal/simple-dataset cases and introduces programmatic backtracing between downstream claims and upstream code/data.
Performance degrades as goal/data complexity increases, where human copiloting becomes important, so provenance is not sufficient by itself for complex discovery.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Data-driven biomedical analysis/manuscript generation; strongest on simple tasks.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need evidence that provenance chains materially reduce hallucinated claims in more open-ended agentic science.

candidate_mechanisms.mechanism: Workflow-architecture optimization should be evaluated independently from raw compute scaling.
evidence: MLReplicate reports the cheapest/fastest system outperformed the most resource-intensive system in human evaluation despite a 38x input-token gap.

ASI-Bench shows cost is not monotonic with autonomous score: GPT-5.6 xhigh B3 is about 40.86 at ~$684/run, Claude Opus 5 + Claude Code about 40.70 at ~$2728/run, while GPT-5.6 ultra reaches 51.60 at ~$1550/run.
Within a fixed strong configuration, more reasoning can still matter: ASI-Bench GPT-5.6 xhigh->ultra raises B3 40.86->51.60.
candidate_mechanisms.scope: Cross-system comparisons are confounded by model and capability differences; this is evidence against 'more compute alone' as a general predictor, not against test-time scaling within a fixed workflow.
candidate_mechanisms.uncertainty: Need matched workflow/compute scaling curves to locate where extra budget helps versus where architecture dominates.

negative_and_boundary_evidence: ASI-Bench: average autonomous score without method guidance is 26.62; only the best B3 configuration in the reported set exceeds 50, at 51.60.
AIRS-Bench: aggregate valid-submission rate is about 59.3%; research-task performance remains very low on expert tasks, and Greedy does not universally dominate ReAct there.
ResearchClawBench: strongest baseline autonomous agent averages 21.5 against a 50-point target-paper rediscovery anchor across 40 tasks / 10 domains.
ARAC-Bench: best end-to-end alignment/completeness score among evaluated frameworks is 67.9/100; experiment is the primary stage bottleneck.

MLReplicate: 3/48 targeted runs failed to produce output, 8 were desk-rejected for insufficient length, only 10/37 valid submissions were auto-accepted, and no system was reliably publication-ready under human review.
MLReplicate: fabricated or unsupported claims appeared in 59% of automated acceptances; overall AI-vs-human rating correlation is weak (Pearson 0.29).

MLReplicate limitation: underlying experiments were not validated for all generated manuscripts, so reported hallucination/reproducibility findings should not be generalized as a full code-level reproduction audit.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Treat method selection as the main ASI-Bench bottleneck.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Revised/rejected: B1->B2 (full procedure removed, method kept) loses 21.82 points, while B2->B3 (method hint also removed) loses only 2.48; procedure synthesis is the larger diagnosed gap.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Claim best-first tree search universally dominates ReAct.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Rejected as universal claim: Greedy dominates many AIRS slices, but the expert slice under one reported transform has ReAct 0.10 vs Greedy 0.04; model/scaffold budgets are not fully matched.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Use automated conference acceptance as a scientific-validity gate.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Rejected as standalone gate: MLReplicate finds weak overall AI-human rating alignment and 59% fabricated/unsupported claims among automated acceptances.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Assume additional tokens/compute monotonically improve autonomous scientific quality.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Rejected across systems: MLReplicate shows a 38x token gap without quality ordering. Retain narrower within-workflow test-time-scaling hypotheses where matched evidence supports them.

rejected_or_deferred_leads.lead: Treat academic skill packages as solving the experiment bottleneck.
rejected_or_deferred_leads.reason: Deferred/qualified: ARAC shows proposal/synthesis improvements but no significant Experiment improvement; some benchmark/coding dimensions regress.

Extract matched same-model AIRS-Bench Greedy vs One-Shot/ReAct results and compute/node budgets to isolate scaffold causality; preserve expert-task exception.

Inspect the full ARAC skill-package repositories/papers to decompose AR-Skill/Arbor/AIR-Skill/SA-Skill into atomic components and identify which gains are retrieval, validation, formatting, or reasoning.
Inspect Data-to-paper supplementary experiments for exact simple-vs-complex task breakdown and whether provenance/backtracing measurably reduces claim errors.

Search for self-generated inspiration/pivot mechanisms that can create useful sparse research clues without target leakage, and compare them against retrieval-only idea generation.
Search for prospective plan-execution contract checkers or procedure compilers in scientist agents, especially interventions evaluated end-to-end rather than inferred from failure analysis.
